channel.title: casualdata daily
channel.description: casualdata publishes one new interactive data visualization every day: a chart, map or picture of the day's news and data, each on its own dated page with its sources. It also keeps casualdata's data visualization art projects from 2007 to 2011.

item.title: Russia, the United States and China hold 91 of every 100 nuclear warheads in the world. Their three leaders met together for the first time on 19 November 2026
item.description: A square of 12,187 dots, one for each nuclear warhead in the world at the start of 2026, cut into nine blocks by country. Russia holds an estimated 5,420, the United States 5,042 and China 620: together 11,082, or 91 of every 100. Six other countries hold the rest.

item.title: In Niger, 66 of every 100 people have no toilet to use. No country has a higher share
item.description: A dumbbell chart of the share of people with no toilet to use (open defecation) in 2000 and in 2024, in the 27 countries where it is still 10 in every 100 or more, and in India. Niger is highest of 195 countries: 66 in every 100 people in 2024, down from 81 in 2000. India went from 73 to 7.

item.title: The US dollar has fallen 7.5% against the Korean won since 2 January 2026. It has risen against 24 of 29 currencies
item.description: Twenty-nine small line charts, one per currency, show how much of each currency a US dollar buys on every day from 2 January to 17 November 2026, as the change since 2 January. On 17 November a dollar bought more than on 2 January in 24 of the 29 currencies, most of all the Turkish lira, up 17.2%, and less in 5, least of all the Korean won, down 7.5%.

item.title: France ordered 137,550 people to leave in 2025, more than twice as many as any other EU country. 18,930 people left France after an order
item.description: A map of Europe with one circle per country, sized by how many people it ordered to leave in 2025, with a dark core for how many left after an order to leave. The EU 27 ordered 486,705 people to leave and 156,000 left. France gave the most orders, 137,550, more than twice Germany’s 55,240, and 18,930 people left France after an order.

item.title: Türkiye made less than a third of its electricity from fossil fuels in April, May and June 2026. No other month since 2018 did
item.description: Türkiye’s electricity, each month from January 2018 to September 2026, as a grid of 105 squares shaded by the share made from coal, gas and oil. Only April, May and June 2026 were under a third (29.3%, 27.3% and 31.6%); the next lowest month was April 2020 at 34.3%. With each month’s mix of fossil, hydro, wind and solar and other renewables.

item.title: Wales lost to New Zealand 34 times in a row. On 14 November they won, 35–28
item.description: All 39 rugby union matches between Wales and New Zealand, 1905 to 2026, as bars either side of zero: four Welsh wins and 35 defeats, 34 of them in a row from 1963 to 2025, before Wales won 35–28 in Cardiff on 14 November 2026. With each match’s date, ground and score.

item.title: Same city, same ground stop: Dallas-Fort Worth lost 34% of its departures, Love Field 9%
item.description: On 13 November 2026 the FAA halted departures across the US for hours. The share of the day’s departures cancelled at each of 84 US airports, from 6% to LaGuardia’s 41%: Dallas-Fort Worth 34%, Dallas Love Field 9%. With the counts of cancelled and delayed flights.

item.title: A 1960 equation put the world’s population at infinity on 13 November 2026. Until the mid-1990s the world was ahead of it
item.description: The 1960 “Doomsday” equation of von Foerster, Mora and Amiot against the world’s population, year by year from 1700 to 2026: the population ran above the equation until the mid-1990s and has been below it since.

item.title: India more than halved its child pneumonia deaths. Nigeria’s have barely moved
item.description: Estimated deaths of children under five from pneumonia in 2015 and 2024, for the six countries that lose the most: India’s fell from about 179,000 to about 70,000, while Nigeria’s stayed near 150,000. UNICEF estimates.

item.title: No El Niño week on record was as far above normal as the last seven
item.description: Weekly sea-surface temperature in the central Pacific (Niño 3.4), in degrees above the 1991–2020 normal: for seven weeks running, to the week of 4 November 2026, it has been above +3.0 °C, the highest week before this year in NOAA's record, which starts in 1981.

item.title: CO₂ has been higher at every climate summit than at the one before
item.description: Carbon dioxide in the air in the month each of the 31 UN climate summits opened, from Berlin in 1995 (360 ppm) to Antalya in 2026 (430 ppm), measured at Mauna Loa with the seasonal cycle removed: it was higher at every summit than at the one before.

item.title: Every forecast miss went the same way
item.description: All 435 House seats of the 2026 midterms, placed by how forecasters rated them before the election and shaded by who won: Democrats took 21 seats rated Republican and every toss-up, and Republicans took none rated Democratic.

item.title: 99 votes may decide a seat in Congress
item.description: The five closest races of the 2026 midterms, drawn as crowds side by side: one figure for every vote of the lead.

item.title: Voters split by issue, not by party
item.description: Every 2026 ballot measure on a party issue, grouped by issue, against how the same state voted for president. Abortion rights ran ahead of Democrats everywhere; transgender limits ran ahead of Republicans everywhere.

item.title: If the country were 100 people, 51 of them stayed home
item.description: The 2026 midterm electorate as a town of 100 people: who voted, for which party, and who stayed home.

item.title: Nearly every Senate race moved toward the Democrats
item.description: Each 2026 Senate race against the same state's 2024 vote for president. 30 of 31 moved toward the Democrats. The exception was Maine.

item.title: Where the light goes in November
item.description: Hours of daylight for every latitude, every day of the year. Point anywhere to read it.

item.title: In the time it took to win this year’s Route du Rhum, the first winner had sailed 28% of the way
item.description: Tom Laperche won the 2026 Route du Rhum in 6 days 13 hours 27 minutes. A map of where each of the 13 winners since 1978 would be after that long, at their own average speed: the first, Mike Birch, 998 nautical miles out with 2,544 to go.
